verdict.rationale: OCI release notes document a first-party Select AI Agent Framework in which agent teams are defined, managed and run inside the database and can be shared across schemas. That is a shipped, documented agent orchestration capability, not just a vision. The evidence is a single release-note mention of a database-embedded framework, with no detail on a managed agent runtime, hosting, deployment or lifecycle. OCI Generative AI model import (docs-26) is model hosting, not agent runtime, so it earns no credit here. missing for 10: a documented standalone managed agent runtime/hosting service, in-depth agent orchestration docs (tools, memory, deployment, scaling), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native team, agents have a managed home — first-party agent runtimes/orchestration services shipped and documented, not just a blog vision

citations.quote: You can now share the Select AI Agent Framework teams across database schemas. Define and manage an agent team in one schema, then grant another database user or role permission to run the team
